observations.note: six persistent flags appeared in the 20:35:45->20:37:20 window; at least one is this Korok, the others look like first-time UI/save flags (they stay 1 in every later save)
single new flag: koroks do have a per-object flag; the earlier 'no flag' was a diff-window attribution error

the chest needs a monster hunt cleared first. The player opened it before the 21:18:33 save; that is why the save pair 21:18:33 -> 21:19:42 shows no new flag. The thirteen flags in the 21:17:05 -> 21:18:33 window are therefore a mixed event: monster-hunt completion + reward chest (and possibly first-time flags).

one travel Korok (two seeds) in a 7.5-minute save window: nine new flags, so the delta is mixed with other small events (movement/discoveries) or several flags belong to this Korok type. Compare with the clean korok #2 sample (14-second window, exactly one flag).

伊恩伊萨神庙. None of these equals the first shrine's discovery flag 0x5F6180D7, so discovery is per-shrine. Several counters also moved: 0x16D9641D 0->2, 0x63866C56 7->8, 0x9DD69D5F 10->11, 0xC41B7240 2->3.
余料建造. 0x161D8560 goes 1->2 (a shrine-activation counter, not a per-shrine flag); 0xA04D6D59 1->0
eleven flags in a 1.5-minute window; 0x5976A9AE 0xFFFFFFFF -> 0x0000000B (counter init?)
伊恩伊萨神庙 completion + battery. None of these equals the ten flags of shrine-1 completion, so completion flags are per-shrine too. 0x31AB5580 5->12 (a counter/bitfield).

no table flag; a whole-file diff shows an opaque data blob (0x0D95xx) changed by about 700 bytes. Chest state is therefore in the data section, while the earlier chest 'flag groups' were auxiliary achievements (which is why their size varied).

dataChanges.note: byte-level diff; the real chest state appears to live in this opaque blob

findings.eventModel: an in-game event sets a group of opaque 32-bit flag keys; no flag name or object id is needed to detect it
findings.perObject: chest-1 {0x1BED068D,0x1F23D973,0xAD3CBF08} and chest-2 {0xDBEA8E06,0xF9525C48} do not overlap
findings.korok: korok #2 sets exactly one persistent flag 0xB33C6725; the first korok window also contained five first-time UI/save flags that persist, which is why it looked flagless
findings.counter0x449B3BA6: values run 16..23 then wrap to 0..4 across saves, so it is not an event counter; most likely an in-game hour (0-23) or another time-like field. Earlier 'increments on event X' observations were time passing.
findings.hashMapping: CRC32/CRC32C/Murmur3-32/FNV-1a over 3373 GameDataList names and 666 wiki source_ids do not produce the observed keys
findings.position: the save carries the player position (tag 0xC884818D), so no memory read is needed for the binding step
findings.chestGroups: chest-1 {0x1BED068D,0x1F23D973,0xAD3CBF08} (3), chest-2 {0xDBEA8E06,0xF9525C48} (2), chest-3 {0x1932FAB1,0x2D048130,0x736B8EC3,0x8F4849A7} (4): all disjoint, group size varies; bind the whole group.
findings.firstTimeFlags: some flags are first-time UI/save flags (set once, stay 1): a group can contain more keys than the object needs; bind groups but keep an 'unexpected group size' review state

timeOfDay.note: the player reported the in-game clock at both saves; hour 0x449B3BA6 and minute 0x2106FA19 match exactly

findings.prerequisites: some objects have prerequisites (a reward chest behind a monster hunt). One save delta can then contain several events at once; the wiki binder must treat mixed deltas as multi-event and either split by marker type/position or queue them for review instead of marking one object blindly.
findings.windowLength: the delta can only be as clean as the save interval: korok #2 had 14 s between saves and yielded exactly one flag; the travel korok had 7.5 min and yielded nine, mixing events. The bridge must expose the interval/savedAt and the consumer should treat long windows as multi-event (review queue).
findings.shrineDiscovery: shrine-1 discovery flag 0x5F6180D7; shrine-2 discovery produced six flags, none equal to it: discovery flags are per-shrine, and the group can include first-time flags
findings.counters: 0x161D8560 increments when a shrine is activated (1->2), and 0x16D9641D / 0x63866C56 / 0x9DD69D5F / 0xC41B7240 also increment on discovery - these are counters, not per-object flags
findings.shrineCompletion: shrine-1 completion: ten flags; shrine-2 completion: seven flags, no overlap. Both discovery and completion are per-shrine; the battery reward may add its own flags inside the same delta.
findings.dataBlob: progress.sav contains opaque state blobs; 0x0D9510.. is a list of 8-byte hashes that changes at chest/korok/shrine events and grew at each chest. These 64-bit values do not match the wiki marker source_ids (tested little and big endian). Detecting an event is possible; enumerating which chest is open requires decoding this structure.
